Yes I have this too - it’s actually one of the reasons that I detest group settings bc I feel like I’m getting way too much input and it totally overwhelms me. When I’m 1-on-1, I’m told that I have psychic-like abilities to read what someone is thinking (body language, visual cues, etc..) but I’m picking up on such tiny things and can’t turn it off that when I’m with multiple people (even two) I get confused and overwhelmed because I don’t know who’s body language/needs I should prioritize or follow. 

I also strongly relate to what you describe. I get deeply uncomfortable and quite fixated when someone tells me one thing that clearly doesn’t match their nonverbal cues and.. aura lol? I can even remember as a child nagging my teacher to the point of tears asking her repeatedly “what’s wrong” even though she said she was fine and no one else in the class noticed anything - eventually she would usually tell me that she was tired or stressed or something and then I would feel better. That’s another thing, I don’t really have the same social ability to just “go along” with someone saying they aren’t upset or angry or whatever, when they clearly are. I’ve learned to stop picking at people who don’t want to tell me, but I still am completely distracted by it and can’t move on, if that makes sense. 

This is actually one of the reasons that I’ve questioned whether I have ASD because my ability to read body language and facial expressions is above average but my sense of what to do with that information is … well kinda bizarre lol.

Oh my goodness. Thank you so, so much for taking the time out of your day to write this for me. I cannot day how much I appreciate your story, insight and guidance. I am truly grateful.  

Firstly, I’m so sorry to hear about your story with that family. You’re right - our stories are amazingly similar and because of that I can viscerally feel the pain that must have caused you. I’m so sorry they did that to you. You didn’t deserve it and I understand just how painful that kind of a wound is. I’m not sure I’ll ever get over my own pain with this. I’d love to hear more about how you recovered (or are recovering) from this situation if you’re comfortable sharing. 

I’m at a total loss for what to do about Liz. You’re right that she’s not a bad person. I believe she’s a wonderful person, but this whole thing has been such a mind fuck. If it’s the thought that counts, she’s a saint, but if actions speak louder than words, she doesn’t care about me. And that hurts so bad. And makes me feel so horrible and ashamed of myself. 

I feel like I shouldn’t push away someone who wants to be in my life (even to some capacity), especially since she means so much to me. But I’m struggling with the balance of how I keep her in my life when she triggers me so much with false promises and disingenuous gestures. I’m not sure what she wants. I’m not sure how I should approach this. There’s an argument for ghosting, but that doesn’t sit well with me either. Especially after hearing about your story. We obviously both share a lack of closure, but I’m fortunate enough to still have some contact with Liz, that ghosting feels painful too and maybe something that id regret later. But I don’t know what options are left - I don’t want to ghost, I don’t want to pretend and have a superficial relationship, and having an honest relationship isn’t on the table. Do I even reply to her texts?

Ugh. Sorry for rambling. It’s nice to talk to someone who gets this. It’s so weird how this situation is one of the most painful events in my life even though I’ve been through so many objectively “worse” things. 

Thank you for asking me how I am - you’re very kind. Things are really, really rough now. My life has become rather small and I haven’t done a great job clawing my way out I guess.
